was: Secluded WA DNR campground by a forest stream in the Loomis State Forest, about 10 miles from Loomis via the steep Toats Coulee Road. About 9-11 sites, roughly half pull-through and most good for rigs under 30 ft, vault toilet; no water or hookups. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED as of 2026-09-29: the whole Loomis State Forest was closed for the Sinlahekin Fire. --Claude

was: WA DNR campground in the Teanaway Community Forest north of Cle Elum, in an open pine clearing near the Middle Fork Teanaway River, close to Forest Service trailheads. 11 sites plus group sites (some for horse groups), vault toilet; no hookups. A 25-ft travel trailer is the longest reported. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED as of 2026-09-29: DNR says it remains closed because of flood damage at the access bridge. --Claude

was: Large, open WA DNR campground in the Teanaway Community Forest on North Fork Teanaway Road north of Cle Elum, near the North Fork Teanaway River. 59 roomy sites among ponderosa pine, drinking water, restroom and vault toilets; no hookups or garbage service. Rigs of 30+ ft are reported. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. In 2026 only the south half was open and campfires were banned. --Claude

was: WA DNR campground in Capitol State Forest southwest of Olympia, the main hub for its ~90 miles of motorized trails - expect ORVs. About 24-33 gravel sites in three loops, mostly narrow pull-throughs good for trailers to about 27 ft, vault toilets, camp host; no water or hookups. Season May 1 to late November; 7-day limit. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED for summer 2026 for hazard-tree removal (checked 2026-09-29). --Claude

was: Small WA DNR campground in Loup Loup Canyon west of Okanogan, 3.9 miles up the two-lane dirt Loup Loup Canyon Road from SR-20, near Loup Loup Creek. Eight gravel sites on a loop, drinking water, vault toilet, day-use shelter; no hookups. Popular in hunting season; ATVs on forest roads only. No published length limit - the loop and spurs look long enough for a mid-size trailer. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

was: Small WA DNR campground (also called Sportsman's Camp) in the Loup Loup State Forest, a mile up Sweat Creek Road from SR-20 between Okanogan and Loup Loup Pass. Five sites in an open gravel clearing by a small stream, shelter, vault toilets; no water or hookups. Popular in hunting season; ATVs on forest roads only. One directory lists it as permanently closed while DNR still shows it open - check before relying on it. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

was: Tiny WA DNR campground on quiet, non-motorized Rocky Lake east of Colville, down 2.5 miles of one-lane gravel off Artman-Gibson Road. Five sites among rock formations at the water, drinking water, vault toilet; no hookups. Catch-and-release fishing after June 1. SMALL-RIG CAUTION: one site has taken a 25-ft trailer; the others are hemmed in by rocks. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

was: Illinois Department of Agriculture campground inside Gate 3 at the north end of the Du Quoin State Fairgrounds (off US 51), along the fairgrounds lake: over 1,000 sites with water and 30/50-amp electric, two bathhouses with showers, two dump stations, pavilions, fishing docks. Open April-Oct 31, first come first served (no reservations) outside the late-summer fair. --Claude

was: Idaho Power river-access area just below Swan Falls Dam on the Snake River (Snake River Birds of Prey NCA): 15 designated RV/tent sites, first-come first-served, 14-day limit; vault toilet, fire rings, boat ramp and boarding platform; no water or electric. --Claude

was: Fishlake National Forest campground above Holden: about 10 first-come first-served RV/tent sites in maple and fir at ~7,000 ft, drinking water, vault toilets, open late May to early September, 14-day limit. Reached by 5 miles of narrow, winding gravel Maple Hollow Road from I-15 (second Holden exit) - about 30 minutes; muddy after rain. Campendium's longest reported rig is 34 ft. --Claude

was: Pima County-owned park (concession-run) on Old Spanish Trail east of Vail. RV/car camping first-come first-served, at about 30 individual sites in Posta Quemada canyon (CCC-built picnic areas El Bosquecito and La Selvilla, with tables and grills; water and restrooms there). No hookups. Check in and pay at the Cave Shop first; park hours 8am-4pm and the front gates are locked at night. Pin is the cave parking lot; the camping areas are in the canyon below it and could not be located precisely. --Claude

was: Marina resort on Martinez Lake (Colorado River backwater) north of Yuma. Dry camping 2 weeks $75 or $150/month for 2 people; first-come first-served, pay at the Camp Rental Office. No hookups or marked pads: campers spread out across open desert above the marina, most parked by a shade tree, with roomy, private spacing. Dump station, drinking water, restrooms, showers and laundry nearby; general store sells firewood. --Claude
